Guidance & outlook: Our proposed greenfield facility in Uttar Pradesh will be developed in phases, with Phase I targeted for commissioning in Q3 FY 2027-28 at an initial capacity of approximately 950 million cans per annum, scaling to nearly 1.6 billion cans per annum by FY 2029-30.

OUTLOOK Annual Report 2025-26 Indian Economy The IMF's April 2026 World Economic Outlook estimated India's real GDP growth for FY 2025-26 at ~7 .6%, reflecting strong domestic demand, public capital expenditure and continued momentum across services and manufacturing.

In India, the plastic caps and closures market reached approximately US$ 2.0 billion in 2025 and is expected to grow steadily over the medium term, supported by consumption growth across its principal end-use categories.
Growth & demand: Total income stood at ₹2,760 crore, reflecting 6% Y-o-Y growth, while Profit after Tax increased by 9.2% to ₹352 crore.
This has weighed on growth: the IMF's April 2026 World Economic Outlook now puts global GDP growth at approximately 3.1% for 2026, a deceleration from 3.4% in 2025.

Over the medium-term, global growth is expected to settle at around 3.1% annually, constrained by geo-economic fragmentation, elevated sovereign debt levels, and weak productivity growth outside the technology sector.
Margins & costs: We recycled over 3 lakh tonnes of cullet, enabling approximately 50% recycled-glass utilisation in production and reducing our dependence on virgin raw materials.

This disruption has also stalled disinflation, with global headline inflation forecast to rise to approximately 4.4% in 2026, driven largely by higher energy and crude oil prices following the conflict.
Container glass operated at approximately 95% utilisation and specialty glass at approximately 75%, while realisations benefitted from a higher value-added mix.
Capex & expansion: Construction of our greenfield facility in Gwalior, Madhya Pradesh is progressing as planned and will add 500 tonnes per day of container glass production upon commissioning in March 2027 , increasing our overall capacity by ~25%.
We are further expanding our glass container capacity with a `700 crore greenfield plant in Gwalior, Madhya Pradesh, with 500 TPD capacity and commissioning targeted for March 2027 .

Balance sheet & cash: Rigorous capital management allowed us to reduce net debt by 54% to ₹70 crore, meaningfully strengthening our balance sheet.
This included a voluntary prepayment of ₹193.25 crore towards outstanding term loans in July 2025, funded entirely through internal cash flows, further reducing interest costs.
Reflecting this financial strength, the Board recommended a final dividend of ₹7 per equity share for FY 2025-26, subject to your approval.
Risks & challenges: Volatility in fuel and raw material prices added further pressure on costs across the industry, while disruptions to global trade and energy supplies created additional headwinds.
Growth for FY 2026-27 is projected at ~6.5%, notwithstanding a more challenging environment marked by elevated commodity prices and heightened geopolitical tensions.
